releases.body:
### The exact proposal is visible and reachable

* The Shared tab now shows each proposal's `prop_…` id as a copy chip, so a chat
  reference can be matched to the exact row (and copied back into the room).
* **Open in project** now really lands on that row: the focus ran before the card
  was inserted into the DOM, so the lookup found nothing and the pending id was
  consumed. It focuses after insertion, re-renders when the Shared tab is already
  open and the card is still loading, expands the completed section, and scrolls
  and flashes the row. Chip status lookups are cached for the chat re-renders.

### Proposal references in chat are actionable

* Every `prop_…` named in a PerunChat message is now a chip coloured by its
  status (the project is in the tooltip). Clicking it opens a peek card with the
  project, status, requester, intent, targets and result; **Open in project**
  jumps to the Shared tab, expands the completed section when needed, scrolls to
  the row and flashes it. A new `GET /api/proposals/{id}` resolves a proposal
  across projects, so the operator no longer has to guess which project a chat
  mention belongs to.
* Fixed the **Approve only** confirmation: it referenced an undefined `targets`
  variable and threw before sending the approval.

### Updates refresh the global install

### Updates refresh the global install

* `perun update apply` on a git checkout now re-runs the additive global install
  (`perun install --no-index`) after the pull, so the managed `AGENTS.md` kernel,
  the slash commands and the MCP entry match the release that was just installed.
  Previously only fresh installs and installer upgrades refreshed them, leaving
  git users on old always-on rules. The step backs up before writing and is
  best-effort: a locked or read-only config logs a warning and never fails a
  successful update.

### Global kernel: search with a tool, not a shell pipeline

* The managed global `AGENTS.md` block now tells every project to search with the
  `grep` / `perun_grep` tool and never with a `Select-String` / `findstr` /
  shell-`grep` pipeline. On Windows the console rendering collapses match lines
  into columns of `1`s or ANSI noise, so a search can look empty when it matched
  and a misread costs a whole retry. The template change is applied by
  `perun install` (the global block is refreshed without touching user content).

### Checks hardening (audit follow-up)

* Proposal verification respects the hidden-project rule: a proposal id is no
  longer a side door around `_visible()`, so a session outside a hidden project
  cannot verify its script.
* Check output is treated as untrusted terminal data: OSC/CSI sequences and C0
  control bytes are stripped, and output is decoded as UTF-8 with a console
  codepage fallback (UTF-16 BOM included) instead of a wall of replacement
  characters.
* `project_checks.env` lets the operator add toolchain paths (`JAVA_HOME`,
  `GOROOT`, `NODE_PATH`, …) per check, from the CLI (`--env KEY=VALUE`), the API
  and the dashboard. The runner still starts from a scrubbed base; the common
  toolchain roots are now inherited too.
* `check_runs` keeps the newest 200 finished runs per project; a machine-wide
  cap of 4 concurrent checks prevents several projects from starting heavy
  checks at once. The HTTP run path is capped at 120 s (MCP 300 s, CLI 600 s),
  and a locked/busy check store degrades to a clear "busy" message.
* The dashboard disables Run while a check is running, the confirmation TTL now
  matches the attention card (4 h), and `perun checks add --help` documents
  `--env` and the `--` escape for a command starting with `-`.
* `memory.search_facts()`, `search_room_facts()` and `search_docs()` no longer
  drop a genuine multi-word lexical match when no embedding is available
  (Ollama down, or a row stored/indexed while it was down). The 0.15 semantic
  cutoff now applies only when the row has a comparable vector; unembedded rows
  use a 0.02 lexical cutoff, which admits a genuine two-word match but still
  filters a single incidental word (the `LIKE` pre-filter can admit one). This
  was the long-standing intermittent `test_memory` failure (a two-word hit
  scored 0.03 against a 0.15 threshold).

### Checks: a bounded way to run a verification

* Perun can now run a **verification command** instead of answering "I have no
  shell access". Two paths exist, both deliberately narrow:
  * **Operator-declared checks** live in Perun's own store (`perun checks add
    <project> <name> "<command>"`), never in the project tree, so no room
    message, agent tool or approved proposal can add one. `perun checks list /
    run / remove / history` manage them; the guard MCP server exposes
    `guard_list_checks` and `guard_run_check` (a name, never a command), and the
    Perun MCP server exposes `perun_list_checks` and `perun_run_check`. A check
    may pin a script's sha256 (`--pin tests/check_manifest.py`): the run is
    refused when the reviewed file changed.
  * **Proposal verification** (`perun_verify_proposal`) runs an *executed*
    proposal's approved script (`.py`, `.ps1`, `.sh`, `.bat`, `.cmd`). The
    command is derived from the target, never taken from proposal text; the
    operator sees the exact command and sha256 in the attention card and must
    confirm; the run is refused if the file changes after they answer.
* The operator's confirmation is durable: `check_confirmations` remembers the
  card, so an answer that lands after the room's short wait window is reused by
  the next call instead of asking a second time. A confirmation is one-shot and
  bound to the sha256 the operator saw.
* Every run is cross-process single-flight per project, records its exit code,
  duration and capped output in `check_runs`, logs a `check_ok` / `check_failed`
  / `check_timeout` activity row, runs with the project root as cwd, and gets a
  scrubbed environment (no Perun or provider credentials).
* New HTTP endpoints (`GET/POST /api/projects/{slug}/checks`, `DELETE .../{name}`,
  `POST .../{name}/run`, `GET .../{name}/history`) expose the same store to the
  dashboard.

### Focus lookup hardening

* The session-title lookup is capped at 1 s per call and cached for 30 s, so a
  Focus click stays responsive even when the OpenCode service is slow; a failing
  lookup simply falls back to the project-name hint.
* `config.is_internal_path()` compares real paths, so a symlinked companion repo
  is still recognised; the two startup sweeps are isolated, so one failing cannot
  skip the other; and the terminal-title fallback ignores hints shorter than
  three characters (a project named "ai" cannot select an "ai-playground"
  terminal).

### The private companion repo is not a project

* Discovery could register `perun_internal` — the owner-only companion repo, a
  sibling of the public checkout — as a normal project once the control path
  stopped aborting the scan, producing a second "Perun" card. The registry never
  lists it now, not even with `include_hidden=true` (which the owner's workspace
  uses), directory scans skip it (`config.is_internal_path()`,
  `PERUN_INTERNAL_ROOT` overrides), and a startup sweep marks any row an earlier
  scan created as hidden — never deleted, so its sessions and memory stay. It is
  still addressable by slug.

### Focus finds Windows Terminal sessions again

* On Windows 11 the default terminal hosts a console in a pseudoconsole: the
  terminal window is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of the shell, so the
  project card's Focus button reported "no terminal window found". The run's
  OpenCode **session title** — the text the Windows Terminal tab already shows —
  is now a strong matching hint, and a terminal-class window may fall back to the
  project name (a browser window with the same words never qualifies).
* The session-title lookup uses the service only when discovery has already
  resolved it (`OpenCodeAPI.ready`), so a Focus click never blocks on CLI
  discovery.

### Release-pipeline and dashboard hardening

* `tools/release.py` re-verifies the private owner-workspace marker after the
  reverse sync (`verify_internal_marker()`), so a release cannot half-apply
  version/docs changes and then discover it lost the marker; both checks are
  unit-tested.
* The dashboard's run filter is a pure `visibleRuns(runs, projects)` helper in
  `card_controls.js` (unit-tested), and presence falls back safely when an old
  cached module lacks it. A checkout with only `.git` (a plain public clone) is
  explicitly tested as **not** an owner workspace.
* Docs: the raw-API and Telegram visibility rules for the control project are
  stated explicitly, and the marker file notes that copying it makes another
  checkout an owner workspace.

### The control project is listed only in the owner's workspace

* v0.10.54 gated hidden projects on "this installation has an owner" (a name or a
  paired Telegram chat). That was still per-install: once anyone named or paired,
  the dashboard listed the Perun project. The gate is now a **workspace marker**,
  `.perun/owner-workspace`, shipped by the private `perun_internal` overlay only.
  A checkout carrying that overlay lists the control project; an installed copy
  — and a plain clone of the public repo, which has no `.perun/` — lists user
  projects only. `PERUN_SHOW_HIDDEN_PROJECTS=1` / `0` overrides per process.
* The orchestrator is untouched: the control row stays registered (hidden),
  `/api/health` still reports it, and a run without a project still targets it;
  the Orchestrator page works with zero listed projects. The Agent Console
  picker and the dashboard's "Working now" panel follow the same listing rule,
  so a control-plane run no longer advertises itself there on an installed copy.
* The release pipeline verifies the marker before writing anything and again
  after the reverse sync (`tools/release.py`), so a release cannot silently
  delete it and hide the project on the owner's own dashboard. The installer
  excludes `.perun/`, so no installed copy ships the marker; nothing in the
  installer or `.gitignore` changes.
